inlines.v: DISOBLIGE, verb transitive [dis and oblige.] 1. To do an act which contravenes the will or desires of another; to offend by an act of unkindness or incivility; to injure in a slight degree; a term by which offense is tenderly expressed. My plan has given offense to some gentlemen, whom it would not be very safe to disoblige 2. To release from obligation. [Not used.]
